event.summary: Replacement test reference does not demonstrate the named cross-realm Array.from technique
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
A test comment now points readers to an example that does not contain the specific technique it names. No user-facing failure is established.

## Details
The assigned patch changes events.test.js:145 to say its local-realm reconstruction is the same dodge paste-sanitizer.test.js makes with Array.from. Read the complete replacement test at this commit (lines 1–60): it uses node:vm and checks the browser export, but has no Array.from or cross-realm array assertions. Its header does explain node --test and node:vm, so the other updated references to that header remain supported. This is a misleading example reference, not a change to the event tests or runtime code. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed from source; no execution performed. proposed_drop: do not report this isolated comment-example mismatch as a security/correctness finding because it does not alter a contract, obscure a changed invariant, or establish a user consequence; the surrounding events.test.js comment itself explains the cross-realm reason. Could-be-highest: false; no security or loss-of-work route. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched.

event.summary: Cross-realm test comment points to an example that does not exist
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
The event-feed test sends future maintainers to a paste-sanitizer test for a cross-realm array technique that the referenced test does not use. Its explanation of the test harness now contains a false example.

## Details
The commit's actual patch changes events.test.js:145 from term-bytes.test.js to paste-sanitizer.test.js while retaining the claim that the referenced file uses Array.from to rebuild a value in the assertion's own realm. events.test.js:140–150 explains that objects produced by node:vm have a different Object.prototype and reconstructs each report with a local object spread. The complete paste-sanitizer.test.js at this revision (lines 1–60), reread during synthesis, contains no Array.from, cross-realm array reconstruction, or structural comparison of a sandbox-created array/object. Its VM test at lines 46–59 calls sanitizePastedText and compares only a function's typeof and a returned primitive string. The referenced example is therefore materially false, not merely absent explanatory detail. Remove the specific Array.from/example assertion, or point it to a real test that demonstrates that technique; the existing local explanation of the report reconstruction can remain.

Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness). Confidence: confirmed by patch attribution and complete referenced-file source, not execution. proposed_drop: false. The previous c1 event proposed omitting this because it changed no runtime contract or user behavior and the local explanation was self-contained; that was a severity/actionability filter, not source refutation, and is superseded. Preserve its original consequence: misleading navigation for readers, with no established runtime failure or security/loss-of-work route. Could-be-highest: false. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources were searched. No reproduction or test execution was performed.

event.summary: Removing the xterm input selector preserves the shipped terminal shortcut boundary
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Considered whether removing the old terminal input selector could make Delete or template-sequence keys reach a terminal program. The remaining selector matches the only terminal input this revision creates.

## Details
Both assigned executable changes remove only .xterm-helper-textarea and retain .grid-terminal-input. grid-terminal.js:364–388 creates a textarea with exactly that class, with no editable descendant requiring a closest match in the template classifier. terminal.js:4313 creates the surface through window.farhelmGridTerminal.create; source searches of terminal.js and lib.rs found no xterm creation path. lib.rs:1742–1762 includes and installs these same shortcut assets. session-action-shortcuts.js:38–53 retains modal, editor, repetition and disabled-button guards; template-shortcuts.js:199–280 retains admission, cancellation, snapshot capture and relay handling. The changed tests retain the terminal-vs-editor distinctions (session-action-shortcuts.test.js:39–49; template-shortcuts.test.js:418–432) and merely adapt their selector model. SPEC.md:3368–3383 requires browser Delete to leave ordinary editors alone and both shortcut families to work from terminal input; SPEC.md:1251 explicitly says 'The terminal’s input textarea counts as the terminal.' SPEC_impl.md:1506–1514 says 'Every terminal runs in a terminal host' and the browser 'draws a grid stream with its own grid client'. The removal is consistent with the replacement's contract; no regression route is established. Suggested bucket if there had been a shortcut regression: high/material UX. Confidence: confirmed from source; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation, the only created keyboard target retains the matched class and all other selector behavior is unchanged. Could-be-highest: false for this considered route; no change to deletion confirmation or target binding and no established security/loss-of-work consequence. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched.

event.summary: Grid input and surviving tests support the narrowed shortcut selectors
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Rechecked the suspected regression: removing the old terminal selector does not exclude the shipped terminal keyboard target. Delete and template-sequence input interception still reaches the retained grid textarea.

## Details
The original possible consequence was Delete or template-sequence keys being forwarded to a terminal program after selector narrowing. Synthesis checked the real DOM and its input path, beyond the test doubles: grid-terminal.js:367–368 creates a textarea with class grid-terminal-input; lines 1511–1534 attach the keydown and typed-input handlers to that same input; lines 1871–1872 focus that input. terminal.js:3389 invokes createGridSurface and :4313 creates the grid component. A textarea has no editable element descendant whose event target would require replacing the template helper's matches with closest. Both changed selectors retain this exact class; the session helper additionally uses closest. The guards run in window capture and stop propagation before the input target's keydown handler; no retained class or event-path mismatch was found.

Remaining test source: session-action-shortcuts.test.js:39–49 still distinguishes terminal proxy, ordinary input, contenteditable, non-editor and null targets; :52–79 covers capture registration, disabled/missing controls and repeat suppression in the Mac installer. template-shortcuts.test.js:159–179 models the exact retained selector and ancestor editability; :418–432 asserts ordinary editors yield while a terminal textarea can begin. These are fabricated DOM tests, so they alone do not establish the shipped class. The independent source check above establishes it. Browser helper e2e/tests/helpers/term.ts:22–36 selects that same real class. e2e/tests/session-action-shortcuts.spec.ts:16–27 establishes focused live attachment; :35–77 describes the actual browser chord, ordinary confirmation, focus handback and exact non-forwarding assertion; :137–187 covers modal/editor yielding. e2e/tests/quick-launch.spec.ts:349–419 establishes terminal focus, begins a sequence with Control+Shift+KeyX, composes a launch and asserts no program input. Read these tests as source only; no pass or runtime behavior was observed.

Contract: SPEC.md:1251 exactly says "The terminal's input textarea counts as the terminal." SPEC.md:3371 says "The browser chord leaves text editors other than the terminal alone. A visible modal keeps keyboard ownership." The changed selectors agree with both. The original event's typographic apostrophe in the first quote is corrected here. Suggested bucket for the suspected shortcut regression would be high/material UX; no such regression is established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the proposed input-target mismatch, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation as above; this remains a proposed disposition for the parent, with the original proposal preserved in the append-only history. No accepted drop is claimed. Could-be-highest: false for the considered route; no established security or loss-of-work effect, and deletion confirmation/target binding is unchanged by these patches. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. No readily checkable premise remains open for c2.
